title: RAW one occurrence retains its identity across differently ordered visual and auditory access
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. The owned thunder paragraph explains earlier seeing versus later hearing and compares seeing a woodcutter's stroke with hearing the noise of that same stroke. A common occurrence and the observer's order of access must remain distinct; simultaneous lightning/thunder production is not asserted.

source.work: Robert Steele, Mediaeval Lore from Bartholomew Anglicus, selected and modernized excerpts from Trevisa's translation
source.owned_unit: Complete edited chapter I MEDIAEVAL SCIENCE, id00045 inclusive through id00109 exclusive, including its ending. Editorial introduction was separately read for provenance.
source.locus: Entire thunder paragraph id00088, from the double-vapour account through the final woodcutting comparison, within the complete owned chapter.
source.source_limit: Steele's selection and modernization remain. This is not a complete medieval meteorological book, a new collation, a modern physical explanation, a measured delay, or a target observation.

design.working_hypothesis: A written account can retain an occurrence while distinguishing how and when an observer accesses its aspects. The strongest explicit ownership is the woodcutting comparison: a man sees a stroke before hearing the noise of the stroke. The surrounding lightning/thunder contrast assigns the difference to brightness and the relative subtlety of the faculties, as historical source claims.

input_intermediate_output.input: A woodcutter strikes a tree; an observing person is the subject of seeing and hearing in the comparison.
input_intermediate_output.intermediate: The visually accessed stroke and the audible noise are linked by the repeated stroke referent, while their modes of access remain different.
input_intermediate_output.output: The observer sees the stroke sooner than hearing its noise. The account must preserve the access order without multiplying the stroke into two unrelated blows.
input_intermediate_output.written_explanation: The preceding thunder/lightning case says lightning is sooner seen because it is clear and bright and thunder comes later to the ears because sight is more subtle than hearing. The following As introduces the woodcutting comparison.
input_intermediate_output.limits: The passage does not explicitly establish simultaneous generation of lightning and thunder, a common instantaneous cause for every preceding vapour/wind detail, numerical propagation speeds, measured distance or a delay law. Do not replace its stated historical explanation with modern acoustics.

connected_content_obligations: Retain the observer as owner of the two perceptual relations, while the woodcutter remains owner of the strike. The roles need not be collapsed into one person.
Keep the heard noise attached to the same stroke that was seen; a second unrelated blow is not licensed by the comparison.
Distinguish earlier seeing/later hearing from a claim that the external stroke itself occurred twice in that order.
Preserve the analogy's limited force. It illustrates the perceptual ordering; it does not independently prove simultaneous lightning/thunder generation or every detail of the cloud-rupture account.

Retain the whole source paragraph: hot/dry vapour, watery cloud, storm seeking passage, rupture/noise, bladder analogy, lightning with thunder, the stated sensory explanation and the final stroke comparison. These are not automatically one fully specified modern causal mechanism.
design.distinguishing_consequence: A content account that binds the visible stroke and the heard noise to unrelated occurrences loses the source's repeated ownership. An account that converts the comparative order of seeing/hearing into an obligatory order of distinct external events also changes the source relation. Naming light, sound, sight and hearing alone cannot choose between these accounts.

rivals.name: Two successive external occurrences
rivals.account: A visual event happens first and a separate sound event happens later, without retained common-event ownership.
rivals.contrast: This can mimic the surface sequence but fails the same-stroke relation in the analogy. The lightning/thunder case alone does not settle every production-time question.

rivals.name: Unordered sensory inventory
rivals.account: The passage merely lists things that can be seen and heard.
rivals.contrast: It omits the explicit sooner/later relation, its faculty-based explanation and the repeated stroke referent.

rivals.name: Independent complete perceptual clauses
rivals.account: Full clauses state the common occurrence, observer and temporal comparison without a reusable composition rule.
rivals.contrast: This remains source-compatible. Reuse would require a future written dependency, not source paraphrase alone.
